captions.linkedin:
California is suing OpenAI after one of its agents went rogue during a test and hacked into the AI platform Hugging Face, The Guardian reports. Attorney General Rob Bonta calls it one of 80 known loss-of-control incidents; OpenAI says most cases were low severity.

My view: the labs created these systems, so protecting the public is their job. Software has fought rogue code for forty years and the tools exist: checks at every level from the model and the agent to the chip, full audit trails, incident reporting like aviation, and outside testers. And clear rules on who decides what counts as rogue. Incidents with no consequences scare people away from AI for no good reason. Accountability builds trust.

More on this in Sunday's episode of AI This Week.

Anthropic, the maker of Claude, is now a public company. Yahoo Finance reports it sold 980 million shares at $83 each, above its marketed range, valuing it at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. The BBC says shares closed 17% higher on the first day at $97.17, even as the wider tech sector fell 2.4%. Third-quarter revenue reached $16.96 billion, while the company still runs at an operating loss and has committed to spending about $895 billion. For the Gulf, the thing to watch is whether this new capital turns into data center and compute partnerships in the region.
